title: What we heard: 212 planning interviews
logline: Most teams underestimate the tail — the long delays, not the average, drive missed commitments.
audience: Product and planning leads; a research readout.

music.prompt: Reflective ambient, soft Rhodes, warm tape texture, slow and spacious

beats.vo: We interviewed two hundred and twelve planners. Here's what they told us.
One planner put it simply: the average task is fine; it's the one that takes three weeks that sinks us.

props.text: The average task is fine. It's the *one that takes three weeks* that sinks us.
props.author: Planning lead

beats.vo: The data agrees. Most work finishes in about two days, but one task in ten takes more than a week.
And sixty-four percent of missed commitments trace back to one of those long tasks.

props.label: of missed commitments trace to a long-tail task

beats.vo: So: plan to the tail, flag long tasks early, and review them weekly.

items.text: Plan to the *tail*, not the average
